3.0.notes: Initial public baseline release. The full system-table schema is created by the single 3.0_baseline database migration (Admin → Migrations → Initialize System Tables); there is no earlier release to upgrade from, so no files or config keys are removed. Subsequent releases append their own file/config cleanup entries below this one.

3.1.notes: Added per-table record image galleries with grid thumbnails and edit-form upload. Extended the automation webhook action into a full outbound integration path for n8n / Make / custom receivers: the After delete trigger now fires (rules see the pre-delete row snapshot), PATCH and DELETE methods were added, the JSON envelope carries old_data on update and delete, custom request headers are supported for receiver-side auth, and failed sends can retry once or twice on timeouts and 5xx/429. Webhook signing secrets and custom header values are now stored encrypted (secret_enc / headers_enc) and are never returned to the browser; rules saved earlier keep working from their plaintext secret / headers fields and are re-encrypted on the next save, so no configuration keys are removed. Fixed JavaScript cache busting across both the admin panel and the frontend: an import map now gives every ES module in each tree the same version, so after an upgrade the browser refetches all of them instead of only the entry files. Previously any change to a non-entry module stayed invisible until the user manually hard-refreshed. Adds the 3.1_table_comments database migration, which applies COMMENT ON TABLE / COMMENT ON COLUMN descriptions to every spw_* table (metadata only, no structural change) - run Admin -> Migrations -> Initialize System Tables to apply it. Note reminders (User menu -> Notes) now take a date and time instead of a date only; the 3.1_notes_reminder_time migration widens spw_notes.reminder_date from date to timestamp (existing reminders keep their day at 00:00) and the notification cron delivers a reminder once that moment has passed.

3.2.notes: Adds per-user access control for tables, views and printouts, gated by default at the API boundary so record listing, delegated FK lookups, workflow runs and the schema/files endpoints are all scoped to what the current user is allowed to see; builds on the existing spw_record_owners ownership history and spw_users access-scope settings, so no new tables or columns are required and there is no database migration to run. Views Sync now discovers materialized views alongside regular views, and RAG accepts materialized views as aggregate views (flagged as such in the docs UI). Adds shared os_api_action()/os_api_dispatch() request handling, used by the comments, files, notes and owners API endpoints. No files, config keys or database schema changes are removed by this release.

3.3.notes: User accounts can now carry optional contact details - first name, last name, email address and phone number - entered in Admin -> Users -> Manage Users, either in the Add New User form or through the per-row Edit Details dialog, and shown in the new Name / Email / Phone columns. The data is informational and admin-panel exclusive: nothing on the frontend reads it, it is never returned by the public API, and it plays no part in login, ownership or notifications. All four fields may stay empty; the email is checked for a valid format only and is not required to be unique. Adds the 3.3_user_contact database migration, which appends the four nullable columns to spw_users together with their column comments - run Admin -> Migrations -> Initialize System Tables to apply it. Until it is applied the contact fields are simply not offered: the Manage Users tab says which migration to run and otherwise works exactly as before, so listing accounts, activating them, changing roles and resetting passwords are unaffected by the upgrade order. Adds an optional Click Statistics module (Admin -> System -> Click Statistics), disabled by default: while it is off nothing is emitted into the page, no collector script is loaded and no request is made, so the application behaves exactly as it did before. When switched on, clicks on buttons, links and elements carrying a data-stat attribute are buffered in the browser and delivered in batches via navigator.sendBeacon to public/api/clickstats.php, which stores who clicked, when, which element, and - when the page has one - the table and record in context. The new spw_clickstats table is created by the 3.3_clickstats database migration; run Admin -> Migrations -> Initialize System Tables to apply it. Recorded clicks expire after a configurable window - 90 days by default, 0 to keep everything - applied by the existing notifications cron, and the module's Log tab additionally trims or clears the log on demand. Adds the spw_config key "clickstats". No files or config keys are removed by this release.

3.4.notes: Replaces the bundled icon set with Material Symbols Outlined. public/assets/icons/material/ now carries the full set - 3899 SVG at optical size 24, with width and height normalised to 48 so they match the intrinsic size of the PNG icons next to them - plus the generated index.json, tags.json and README.txt manifests. The icon field in the admin gets a searchable picker: it matches icon names and the Google tag list, understands common Polish words, offers category chips and remembers recently picked icons in the browser. 84 files were removed from public/assets/icons/ (83 PNG plus chevron-down-white.svg, whose only use, the dropdown arrow on select elements, is now an inline data URI in public/assets/css/styles.css); every reference inside the project was repointed at the new set, and eight PNG icons that the system still names directly (book_3s, delete, folder_zip, grid_on, notifications, picture_as_pdf, search, settings) stay where they are. IMPORTANT for upgrades: icon paths are stored in the database, not in code - the menu_icon keys of the dashboard, calendar, files, board, views and workflows config, the per-table icon in the schema config, and the printout icons. A stored path naming one of the removed files stays valid as far as validation is concerned and renders as a broken image; nothing rewrites those values automatically. Repoint them in the admin with the Browse picker - 79 of the 84 removed names have an identically named .svg under assets/icons/material/, so assets/icons/NAME.png usually becomes assets/icons/material/NAME.svg. The exceptions are calendar.png (use calendar_month.svg) and folder_zip_blue.png, grid_on_blue.png, picture_as_pdf_blue.png, which have no direct counterpart. Removing the listed files is safe once no stored configuration still names them. No database migration and no configuration keys are removed by this release.

3.5.notes: Adds a language selector to the login page so users can pick their locale before signing in. The notes UI strings are now translated into all 19 locales. The notifications dropdown shows a timestamp on each item and its panel is unified with the bp-panel style. Edit and create forms gain searchable foreign-key pickers (fk-search.js) instead of a plain select. A GitHub link is added to the footer, and the #debug bar no longer flashes before JS hides it on page load. No database migration and no configuration keys are removed by this release.

3.6.notes: Adds an External API module (Admin -> System -> API): admins define read-only API keys, each bound to one schema table with a chosen column set, fixed server-side filters and a row limit. The configuration lives in the spw_config external_api key; keys are stored encrypted (key_enc) plus an HMAC key_hash for constant-time lookup, and are never returned to the browser after generation. External services call public/api/external.php with the key as an Authorization: Bearer header and receive JSON rows; the endpoint accepts no table, column or filter names from the client, refuses hidden and system tables, is rate-limited per key and per IP, and answers 401/403/404/429. No database migration and no configuration keys are removed by this release.
